Craft at the scale of a building

Windows, eaves and small signs of care

Painted windows, chimneys, a carved vent, climbing ivy and a wrought lantern fit the buildings’ existing detail positions. These enlarged previews expose the workmanship; in the world, each piece fits its actual window, roof or wall.

Loading the architectural details…

The accents follow each building’s established outline and material. They preserve real doors and approaches. Larger authored facade views remain a separate next art batch.

The larger natural shapes

Rooted canopies, regional silhouettes

These trees use their measured root anchors and normal game proportions. Sable stands beside each at a fixed 60-pixel reference height, making a broad crown, a bent upland tree and a low orchard canopy easy to compare.

Loading the canopy collection…

Tree selection uses the region’s existing safe scenic sites. The live renderer fades a foreground canopy when it covers a traveller; the gallery keeps each silhouette fully visible for inspection. The prop-scale slider above applies to the smaller object collections.

The continuous ground layer

Materials under every step

Eight painted surfaces bring fine moss, mineral grains, frost and mycelium into each region. These previews use the same restrained blend and mirrored repeat as the game, over its regional ground colors.

Loading the painted material sheet…

Four quieter kinds of water

Alluvial rivers, root-darkened tides, coral shallows and pale saltglass water each have their own painted depth and color. These cards use the production water layer over its matching base.

Loading the regional water sheet…

The slow drift is an inspection aid; the game’s ground stays still as the camera moves. Reflected repeats keep adjacent image edges aligned. Surface grain stays subdued beneath the larger scenery, while water uses its own quiet regional treatment.

Reading the collection

Scenery variants occupy existing safe edge sites and use the district’s material and ecology. Furniture replaces matching existing household objects. Ground details stay beneath the characters. This gallery lists the complete kit; an individual location selects only the motifs appropriate to that place. A motif marked Staged is prepared for a future authored placement and is not scattered into ordinary scenes.

The cross marks the object’s bottom-center registration point. Painted shadows and irregular silhouettes retain the source image’s alpha channel. Adjust the scale or enable the checker to inspect their edges. Scenery props use the same painted sheets in Standard and Compatibility. Facade accents appear in Standard’s detailed building rendering.

Review pages do not read or write your journey saves. Scenery does not create new collision, exits or quests. Objects with an established story function keep their own artwork and interactions.
